What graces my pull list this week, you ask? Largely a Marvel week apparently:

  • Moon Girl and Devil Dinosaur #9 - this still remains just a super fun book. lighthearted, great art, and a strong story. Second book in the new story line, so if your LCS still has last week and you were looking to dive in, go for it. Won't miss much if you skipped the first story (which should be out in trade real soon if it isn't already)

  • Ms. Marvel #9 - more Civil War II story. I am not following the rest of that at all but so far this has been able to get enough of the story without requiring me to pick that up so I don't mind it. i was very anti-civil war II to start but so far, this bit of tie in has me interested enough in possibly picking up the collection once it finishes.

  • Venom Space Knight #10 - this one I like for the same reasons as Moon Girl because it is also a ridiculous book that knows it is ridiculous and doesn't take it self too seriously. that said, it could not be more different from Moon Girl as it's the same Flash from previous continuity dealing with the evil from his past and continuing his quest to change.

Got a couple more maybes on my list too but nothing I'll probably pick up for a bit, if at all. I have a tendency to add whatever is new and looks interesting to my wishlist on comixology then periodically look through it after a bunch of reviews have populated. Tends to favor things not making the cut.

Part of this list is also meant to be recommendations of things you feel others should read. With that in mind, I have been rereading Transmetropolitan and I highly recommend you do the same or pick it up for the first time if you never have. Regardless of election year and candidates, that fictional universe election coverage by fictional journalist Spider Jerusalem (written by the very real Warren Ellis) encapsulates the system stupidly well.
